title: Clipboard copy and paste in a desktop app
when: The desktop app copies results such as rows, links or codes for other apps and pastes data from spreadsheets or text editors.
prompt:
Goal: clip.js copies and pastes text through the native clipboard with the right format for other apps and safe parsing of what comes in.
Steps:
1. Copy: await Neutralino.clipboard.writeText(text); fall back to navigator.clipboard.writeText when running in a plain browser.
2. Paste: await Neutralino.clipboard.readText() from a Paste menu item or Mod+V; also handle the "paste" event and read event.clipboardData.getData("text/plain").
3. Copy rows as tab separated values with \n line endings, so spreadsheets split them into cells; quote nothing.
4. Parse pasted tables by splitting lines on \r?\n and cells on \t; trim a trailing empty line; cap at 10,000 rows.
5. Treat pasted text as data: insert with textContent or input values, never innerHTML.
6. Confirm with a short "Copied" status in an aria-live region for 2 seconds.
7. Never read the clipboard on a timer or at start; only on a user action.
8. Allow clipboard.readText and clipboard.writeText only.
Quality bar:
- Copied tables paste into a spreadsheet as cells.
- Pasting HTML from the web never runs scripts.
Pitfalls:
- Reading the clipboard silently, which leaks passwords the user copied.
- Losing leading zeros by converting pasted codes to numbers.
Verify:
- [ ] Copy and paste run inside user actions.
- [ ] Pasted content is inserted with textContent.
- [ ] A status message confirms copy.
Output: clip.js and the Edit menu wiring.

examples.input: copiar a tabela do app e colar na planilha
examples.output: Rows copied as TSV via clipboard.writeText, paste parser for tab cells, textContent insert, aria-live status
